newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Products - Refiners boost Gulf gasoline.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Products - Refiners boost Gulf gasoline.

text.p: U.S. Gulf prompt gasoline prices jumped sharply Wednesday as refiners chased barrels higher ahead of a pipeline deadline there, market players said.
However, New York Harbor and Midcontinent spot market trade remained subdued through the end of the day.
On the NYMEX, June gasoline gained 0.42 cent to close at 65.80 cents a gallon and June heating oil gained 0.12 cent to settle at 55.39 cents a gallon.
Prompt conventional M1 gasoline traded as high as 1.00 cent over the July NYMEX price, traders said, up nearly 1.50 cent from the previous day, before weakening late.
Those M1 barrels were talked between 0.25 and 0.50 cent over the July NYMEX late in the day.

Market traders pointed to active refiner buying ahead of the scheduling deadline on the Colonial Pipeline at the end of the day. The Colonial is the main products artery from the Gulf Coast to the East Coast.
Conventional M1 for scheduled delivery early next week changed hands at 0.50 cents under the July NYMEX, also up about 1.50 cent on the day.
Prompt 93-octane V1 conventional gasoline also gained, increasing the premium to the M1 to about 5.00 cents, according to traders.
Low sulphur diesel rateable barrels traded at about 1.65 cents under the July NYMEX, traders said, while prompt heating oil traded at 2.40 cents under the July NYMEX.
Players said activity in the Harbor was very quiet through the second half of the day, with differentials mostly unchanged from Tuesday's levels.
Some "specialty" barrels of prompt conventional M2 gasoline were heard done at 2.60 cents under the June NYMEX, modestly weaker than estimations of the barge market, traders said.
Prompt heating oil barrels firmed slightly, with players reporting a deal at 0.10 cent under the June futures, up about 0.10 cent from Tuesday.

Midcontinent markets remained thinly traded on Wednesday amid a dearth of fundamental news. Group Three prompt unleaded differentials were steady at about 4.75/5.00 cents over the NYMEX screen. Barrels delivered by June 1 to June 7 were being bid at about 5.00 cents.
"There is not much of a market," said a Midwest player.

Chicago markets were mostly quoting June barrels. A 2.75 cents deal over NYMEX gasoline was done for the first cycle, while a 2.50 cent deal traded for the second cycle. Chicago jet fuel was pegged 3.00/3.25 cents, about a quarter cent higher than Tuesday due to a slight tick up in demand.
